valuation_philosophy.summary: This is NOT a going-concern growth DCF. On 31-Jul-2026 GXH completed the sale of its Medical division (The Doctors, 65 clinics) to Tend Health for a gross NZ$270m, approved by shareholders 99.82% on 14-Jul-2026. GXH is now a pure-play NZ pharmacy retailer (Unichem/Life Pharmacy). At the current price of $1.95, market capitalisation is ~NZ$280.5m against 143,834,147 shares -- almost exactly the gross Medical sale price. The cash/proceeds component is therefore roughly 96% of market cap, and the value of the retained Pharmacy business is a small residual. The correct model is SUM OF PARTS: PV(retained Pharmacy business, owner-FCF DCF) + net Medical sale proceeds (risk-adjusted for the Board's undisclosed capital-allocation decision) + existing net cash, divided by shares outstanding.
valuation_philosophy.why_not_a_cagr_dcf: Every consolidated historical growth rate (revenue, EPS, equity, FCF) blends a Medical division that has now been sold, and pre-Feb-2023 also blends a Community Health division that was sold in FY2023 ($50m EV, $21.8m gain -- which is why FY2023 NetIncome of $45.2m / EPS 31.6c is an outlier). None of that history describes the business that exists today. FY2022's $670.3m revenue is a COVID-era spike, also excluded.
valuation_philosophy.what_the_answer_depends_on: Not pharmacy growth (which is modest, low-single-digit, and margin-pressured by Chemist Warehouse). The answer depends almost entirely on (1) how much of the headline $270m survives net-debt/working-capital adjustments, transaction costs and tax, and (2) what the Board decides to do with it -- a decision that had NOT been announced as of 11-Aug-2026. Bull/Base/Bear scenarios are built around these two capital questions, not around revenue-growth assumptions.
valuation_philosophy.net_proceeds_assumption: The exact net proceeds figure has NOT been disclosed. We estimate a range: conservative $199.2m, mid $223.3m, optimistic $252.2m, built from the $270m headline less an estimated Medical-division lease-liability transfer (~$40m gross, partially deducted), transaction costs (~2% of deal value) and net debt/working-capital true-up/tax leakage. The base scenario uses the mid case.
valuation_philosophy.board_decision_assumption: No capital-return decision has been announced. Bull assumes a large, close-to-full-value special dividend/return of capital (precedented: GXH paid a $40.1m / 28cps special dividend after the Feb-2023 Community Health sale) with disciplined pharmacy reinvestment of the remainder -- proceeds valued near face. Base assumes partial return, partial retention, with a 15% holding-company/uncertainty discount applied to the cash because it is not yet in shareholders' hands and no plan exists. Bear assumes the cash is substantially redeployed into pharmacy acquisitions/diversification at unproven or value-destructive returns -- a 35% discount is applied, the classic post-divestment value-trap outcome.
valuation_philosophy.conclusion: Base case intrinsic value of $1.896/share is essentially IN LINE with the current $1.95 price (-2.8%), consistent with the market having already re-rated the stock (+63% from $1.20 in March 2026 to $1.95) specifically on this news. This model does NOT manufacture large mechanical upside from adding the sale proceeds on top of a business value that still implicitly capitalises the old (larger) earnings base -- see sanity_check below for the explicit double-count test performed.

inputs.net_proceeds_basis: 270.0 gross less: Medical-division lease liabilities transferring with the business (~$40.4m estimated, based on Medical's 38.5% share of group FY2026 lease depreciation, partially deducted per scenario), transaction costs (~2% of deal value), and an allowance for net-debt/working-capital true-up and tax leakage on the gain. NOT company-disclosed -- an estimate; state explicitly this may prove too conservative or too optimistic once completion accounts are finalised.
inputs.existing_group_net_cash_basis: FY2026 year-end (31-Mar-2026) bank debt 19.823 less cash 28.403 = net cash 8.58 (pre-sale, ex-lease). This cash was already on the balance sheet before the Medical sale proceeds were received (sale completed 31-Jul-2026, after FY2026 year-end).

pharmacy_segment_fy2026.note: Segment profit is EBIT-like: post D&A, post IFRS16 lease depreciation, post $0.474m equity-accounted earnings, PRE allocation of the $3.026m group corporate cost.

medical_segment_fy2026_divested.note: GXH divested the MORE profitable division (Medical +33% YoY) and retained the smaller, slower-growing one (Pharmacy +4% YoY revenue, +3.6% profit).

inputs.corporate_cost_note: Previously spread over two divisions; post-sale the overhead is substantially stranded on Pharmacy alone unless management cuts it. 80% allocation assumed (conservative -- could be higher if nothing is cut, or lower if the Board rightsizes corporate cost).
inputs.nci_basis: FY2026: NCI $5.500m of $25.895m group profit after tax = 21.2%. GXH consolidates 50 subsidiaries with non-controlling interests (partly-owned pharmacies, pharmacist-ownership structure) -- this NCI leakage sits almost entirely with the retained Pharmacy business and is deducted from all Pharmacy owner-FCF figures below.
inputs.pharmacy_lease_allocation_basis: Pharmacy's share of group lease depreciation (9.464 of 15.392 = 61.5%) used as the proxy for allocating lease liabilities/principal repayments between Pharmacy and (now-sold) Medical.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K FY2026 cash flow statement; immaterial (0.035% of pharmacy revenue), applied but does not move the answer
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Group reported FCF (OCF 54.613 - CapEx 9.608 = 45.005) does NOT deduct lease principal or SBC and still includes the now-sold Medical division. Owner FCF at group level = 45.005 - 0.192 (SBC) - 13.752 (lease principal) = 31.06m; shown for historical context only -- NOT the DCF driver, since Medical is gone. The DCF driver is the pharmacy-only owner FCF build below.
inputs.interest_income_treatment: Interest income (FY2026 group $0.387m) is immaterial pre-sale and is folded into the segment 'other expenses'/finance lines rather than separately stripped; POST-SALE, once ~$200m+ of cash sits on the balance sheet, interest income will become material and must be stripped from any future FCF-based valuation of the group (it is NOT double-counted here because this model values cash directly via net proceeds, not via a Gordon-growth FCF stream that also earns interest).

historical_growth.note: CONSOLIDATED historical CAGRs are NOT used as the DCF growth driver -- they blend Medical (sold 31-Jul-2026) and, pre-Feb-2023, Community Health (sold Feb-2023, $50m EV, $21.8m gain). They are reported here for transparency only. FY2022 (COVID revenue spike, $670.3m) and FY2023 (divestment-gain-distorted NetIncome $45.2m / EPS 31.6c) are EXCLUDED from all CAGR calculations below as instructed. FY2019 has no financial-statement data in the CSV (absent).
historical_growth.revenue_3yr_cagr_basis: FY2023(493.6, excluded as base)->... using FY2024 503.9 to FY2026 545.976 (2yr) annualised as a proxy since FY2023 itself is excluded: (545.976/503.9)^(1/2)-1 = 4.1%; blended down to 2.1% to reflect FY2024 was still Medical+Pharmacy mixed and not comparable to the future pharmacy-only base.
historical_growth.equity_5yr_cagr: n/a - FY2019 absent from CSV, FY2021 data incomplete for a clean 5yr equity series
historical_growth.eps_note: Consolidated EPS CAGR not meaningful post-divestment; FY2023 EPS (31.6c) is a divestment-gain outlier and must be excluded from any EPS trend.
historical_growth.fcf_note: Consolidated FCF CAGR not meaningful post-divestment for the same reason revenue/EPS CAGRs are not meaningful -- see model_type note.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: pharmacy_segment_revenue_growth_fy2025_to_fy2026 (only clean, business-comparable growth data point available; used as the anchor for Base-case Year-1 growth)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Not applicable in the standard sense -- the divergence here is structural (a smaller, sold-down business) rather than a modelling red flag. Consolidated equity/EPS/revenue CAGRs are NOT comparable to the retained business and are excluded from the growth-rate selection entirely, per the explicit instruction for this ticker.

shared.horizon_rationale: 5 years is appropriate here because the Pharmacy segment is already a mature, low-single-digit-growth business with a stable margin structure (not a ramping high-growth story) -- the year-5 owner-FCF margin (2.4% base) is roughly flat vs year-1 (2.1% base), i.e. margins are not still climbing, so a 5-year explicit build followed by Gordon-growth capitalisation is not understating a maturing margin.

wacc_rationale.nz_smallcap_base: 9.0% (NZ risk-free ~4.5% + equity risk premium, small/mid-cap ~$280m market cap)
wacc_rationale.regulatory_single_payer_premium: +1.5% (pharmacy revenue depends on Te Whatu Ora/PHARMAC Community Pharmacy Services Agreement funding)
wacc_rationale.competitive_disruption_premium: +1.25% (Chemist Warehouse NZ expansion targeting a doubling of store count)
wacc_rationale.capital_allocation_uncertainty_premium: not stacked into the operating WACC -- instead applied directly as a discount to the cash/proceeds component (see capital_allocation_discount below), to avoid double-counting the same risk in two places
wacc_rationale.nci_complexity_premium: +1.0% (partly-owned pharmacy structure, NCI ~21% of group profit)

base.terminal_cap_basis: 10yr GXH group EV/EBITDA history (3 clean data points available: FY2018 9.18x, FY2025 3.73x, FY2026 4.09x -- other years lack EBITDA disclosure in the CSV). Base uses the ~5.7x average of these three.
base.capital_allocation_rationale: Base assumes a partial return of capital / partial reinvestment outcome -- the most likely given management's own stated 'may include retaining some proceeds ... and a distribution' framing. A 15% discount reflects the cash not yet being in shareholders' hands and the absence of an announced plan as of 11-Aug-2026.

bull.terminal_cap_basis: 10yr max (FY2018 9.18x, the richest multiple in the available history, pre-dating the current competitive/regulatory pressure)
bull.capital_allocation_rationale: Large special dividend / return of capital near full value, consistent with the Feb-2023 Community Health sale precedent ($40.1m / 28cps special dividend paid after that divestment), combined with disciplined incremental pharmacy investment (Care & Advice Health Hubs, digital) funding the modestly higher growth/margin path.

bear.terminal_cap_basis: 10yr min (FY2025 3.73x, reflecting the trough multiple the market has actually paid for this business)
bear.capital_allocation_rationale: Classic post-divestment value trap: cash substantially redeployed into pharmacy acquisitions at full/unproven prices or value-destructive diversification, earning below cost of capital; Chemist Warehouse expansion and pharmacy-ownership deregulation compress Pharmacy margins simultaneously (revenue flat to declining, margin -170bp over 5 years).

base.exit_multiple_vs_current: Implied exit multiple (5.7x) is essentially IN LINE with today's group EV/EBITDA (5.73x, bank-debt basis) -- the model does NOT assume multiple expansion.

base.note: Entry price sits close to intrinsic value ($1.896) because most of the value here is realised/near-term cash (existing net cash + Medical proceeds), which is not growth-dependent and therefore not heavily penalised by the 15% hurdle versus the 14.5% WACC used in the terminal value -- the small gap is exactly what the modest Y1-Y5 pharmacy growth (2-3%, well below the 15% hurdle) contributes.

sensitivity.note: Sensitivity is muted relative to a typical growth-company DCF because ~85-90% of base-case equity value comes from existing net cash and Medical sale proceeds (fixed inputs), not from the discounted pharmacy cash-flow stream -- this is expected and correct for a sum-of-parts model dominated by a cash/proceeds component.

probability_weighted.weight_rationale: Bear is weighted above the usual 25% because the Board has made NO capital-allocation commitment as of 11-Aug-2026 and the base rate for undisciplined cash redeployment after a large divestment (across corporate history generally) is meaningfully non-trivial; Base gets the plurality weight as the most likely partial-return outcome consistent with management's own stated framing.

trip_conditions_evaluated: Implied P/E 7.3x vs history: NOT tripped (no clean multi-year adjusted P/E series; 7.3x is below the group current 13.75x)
Implied EV/EBITDA 2.56x vs 1.5x historical max 9.18x: NOT tripped (far below)
Implied P/B: not evaluable — book value is not segment-split in the filings
Base case upside >100% with price in upper half of 10yr range: NOT tripped — base case upside is NEGATIVE (-2.8%) despite the price sitting in the upper portion of the range
sanity_check.diagnosis: The implied EV/EBITDA on the standalone Pharmacy business (2.56x) is WELL BELOW the 10-year historical average (5.67x) and below even the FY2025 trough (3.73x) -- i.e. the base case is NOT manufacturing an inflated pharmacy value; if anything the implied residual pharmacy value looks cheap, which is consistent with (not contradictory to) the base case landing close to fair value once the cash is layered in. No double-count was found.
sanity_check.fix_applied: None required -- the sum-of-parts structure (pharmacy-only revenue/EBITDA base, single addition of net proceeds, no group-level Gordon-growth FCF stream) was designed from the outset to avoid the double-count risk; the check above confirms it holds.
sanity_check.implied_multiples_after_fix: N/A -- no fix was required; multiples shown above are the as-built model's implied multiples.
sanity_check.current_price_position: Current $1.95 sits in the UPPER portion of the 10-year range ($0.71-$2.69) and has already risen ~63% from the March-2026 FY-end close of $1.20, specifically on the Medical-sale announcement/completion. This is flagged as a 'trip' condition per the model instructions: any base case showing large additional upside on top of this re-rating would be suspect.
sanity_check.trip_test_performed: Checked explicitly for double-counting: (1) confirmed interest income is not being both left inside a Gordon-growth FCF stream AND the cash added separately -- this model does not run a Gordon-growth FCF stream on the group at all, it only discounts the smaller Pharmacy-only cash flows, so no interest-income double-count is possible; (2) confirmed the $270m proceeds are added ONCE, net of estimated deductions, and NOT alongside a valuation that still capitalises Medical's $26.042m segment profit anywhere in the pharmacy DCF (the pharmacy DCF projections start from $380.210m Pharmacy-only revenue, explicitly excluding Medical's $165.766m).

implied_multiples_on_retained_pharmacy_b.basis: Market cap $280.5m less existing net cash $8.58m less mid-case effective Medical proceeds $189.81m = $82.1m implied market value of the standalone Pharmacy business
implied_multiples_on_retained_pharmacy_b.implied_p_book: not meaningful standalone (book value not segment-split in filings)

historical_multiples_ex_outliers.note: FY2019-2024 EBITDA not disclosed in the CSV (no clean group EBITDA figure for those years), so only 3 data points are available for the historical range -- FY2018 pre-dates IFRS16 lease capitalisation so is not perfectly comparable to FY2025/26, but is the best available anchor.
historical_multiples_ex_outliers.note_on_group_multiples: Group P/E, P/B, P/S at current price are calculated on the OLD (pre-sale) combined FY2026 financials and will not be meaningful going forward -- shown only as a bridge/reference point.

sanity_check.conclusion: Base case intrinsic value $1.896 vs current $1.95 (-2.8%) is a plausible, non-tripped result: the market has already re-rated the stock close to a reasonable sum-of-parts fair value on the divestment news. The model is not claiming a large mispricing; it is confirming the re-rating was broadly appropriate, with genuine two-sided uncertainty (bear $1.242 / bull $2.601) driven entirely by the unresolved capital-allocation decision.

warnings: Net Medical sale proceeds are NOT company-disclosed as of 11-Aug-2026; the $199.2m/$223.3m/$252.2m range is this model's estimate of adjustments to the $270m gross headline and could be materially wrong once completion accounts are published.
No Board decision on use of proceeds has been announced; the capital-allocation discount (0%/15%/35% by scenario) is a modelling judgment, not a disclosed fact.

Consolidated historical financial data (pre-31-Jul-2026) is NOT representative of the go-forward pharmacy-only business and must not be used for any trend analysis without the explicit segment adjustments made in this model.
Corporate cost stranding (assumed 80% allocated to Pharmacy) is an estimate; management could rightsize corporate overhead post-sale, which would improve the Pharmacy EV in all scenarios.
